title: How Protection Held Over a Granite Ridge Season Pass Bears on the Carry-Forward Fee Base
content:
Where the household holds a Pass and Trip Protection plan written over a season pass on the account, the share of the carry-forward fee base taken on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme election is reduced.

**First.** Where the collective's protection records show a plan written over a season pass on the household account whose claim has been settled, no part of the fee base is taken: the share is 0 per cent.

**Second.** Where those records show such a plan written over a season pass on the household account standing in force or with a claim open, half of the fee base is taken: the share is 50 per cent.

**Otherwise.** In any other case the fee base is not reduced by this rule.

### The plan records this rule reads

The plan is a Pass and Trip Protection record on the same household account whose covered holding is a season pass. What the records must show is the state that plan stands in — a claim settled on it, or the plan standing in force or with a claim open. A protection plan written over lodging, a lesson booking or any holding other than a season pass is not the plan this rule reads, and a plan on another household account is not read at all.

| The plan written over a season pass on the household account | Share of the fee base taken |
| --- | --- |
| its claim has been settled | 0 per cent |
| it stands in force | 50 per cent |
| it has a claim open | 50 per cent |
| no such plan stands on the account | the base is not reduced by this rule |

### Worked on a hypothetical election

An election recorded on a Granite Ridge Local Pass, whose carry-forward fee is 95.00, on a household account whose Pass and Trip Protection plan over that pass stands with a claim open. Half of the fee base is taken, which on a fee base of 95.00 is 47.50. Had the claim on that plan been settled, no part of the fee base would be taken and the figure the protection share produces would be 0.00.
